description: Optional inspiration palette of narrative structural patterns (act-break shapes, beat templates, scene-sequence rhythms). NOT consulted by runtime routing — the primary agent picks structures ad-hoc or selectively opens this file. Full-catalog loading is a contract violation (#206 AC8).

structures.name: Classical three-act page positions
structures.description: Act I to Act II transition at ~25% of total length; midpoint reversal at ~50%; Act II to Act III transition at ~75%; climax in the final 10%. Used by three-act and Save-the-Cat paradigms.

structures.name: Kishōtenketsu page positions
structures.description: ki spans 0-25%, shō spans 25-50%, ten occupies 50-75% (the re-framing twist takes ample room to land), ketsu spans 75-100%. Note: ten is NOT the climax — it's a meaning-shift, not a confrontation peak.

structures.name: Harmon circle 8 stations
structures.description: 8 stations distributed evenly around the circle: stations 1-4 (you, need, go, search) take the first half; stations 5-8 (find, take, return, change) take the second half. Strong rhythm for half-hour episodic TV.

structures.name: Three-cycle try/fail rhythm
structures.description: Three attempts to achieve the goal: first attempt fails on a simple obstacle, second attempt fails on a more complex obstacle that escalates the stakes, third attempt either succeeds at unexpected cost or fails fatally. Commonly used in folktale structure, classic three-act second-act fun-and-games, and procedural-episode structure.

structures.name: TV pilot cold-open + act structure
structures.description: Hook scene before the title card (cold open), then 4 or 5 acts separated by commercial breaks (premium cable often drops act breaks entirely). Cold open establishes tone + hooks the audience; Act 1 introduces the central conflict; Act 4 or 5 resolves the episode's contained question while leaving the season's question open.

structures.name: Frame story
structures.description: Outer narrative brackets an inner narrative — a character tells a story; a journalist investigates an event; a found-document conceit wraps the main plot. Strong fit for stories whose meaning depends on the act of recounting. Used by Heart of Darkness, The Princess Bride, Big Fish.
